title: Macro tables of the 78 first-pass pages, read on the shared TeX tokenizer (V2)
question: Which macros do the math spans of the 78 first-pass pages use, from the rendition's own table or the D2 §12.1 fallback, with which bodies; what does a reader on the token form's TeX tokenizer (\newcommand, \renewcommand, \providecommand, \DeclareMathOperator) read that the spike's pylatexenc reader missed, page by page?
method: code/s5_spans.py regenerates the 78 pages with s1_adapter.adapt under the S1 configuration (contract R1, parser lxml recorded; the stored seven compared and taken as they stand) and keeps every div.latex block; code/s5_macros.py reads the definitions with mathgrammar.printer.tex_tokens (TeX's rules: name, optional [n], optional default, body as TeX reads arguments; \newcommand of a defined name kept first, \renewcommand replaces, \providecommand only when undefined), compares with the spike reader per page, builds each effective table (page over the D2 §12.1 fallback) and counts every control word of every math span by source.

outputs.role: every math span: page, segment key, offsets, kind, delimiting status, LaTeX
per page: rendition key, parser, libxml2, spike reader table, div.latex sources, stored-page identity
per page: tokenizer reader table, what the spike reader missed, effective-table and parser-key comparison
every control word in math: count, pages, source, expansion, differing bodies

results.name: math_spans
results.note: 28,948 delimited ok, 8 partial; equal to s1.corpus; the stored seven pages regenerate identically (text, math spans, macros)

results.name: definitions
results.note: 630 \newcommand, 22 \renewcommand; no \providecommand, \DeclareMathOperator, \def or \let; no macro takes arguments

results.name: pages_where_spike_reader_missed_a_definition
results.note: all \renewcommand{\P}{\mathbb{P}} (\P is a LaTeX built-in, so \renewcommand is the right definer); 803 \P uses took the fallback under the spike reader

results.name: pages_whose_effective_table_differs
results.note: the fallback's \P body is the same; parser classification keys identical too

results.name: names_with_differing_bodies
results.note: \var, \kur, \skw, \sgn: a leading \, on some pages; \kur as \text{kur} on one

results.name: control_words_in_math
results.note: 96 read by the grammar (35,035 uses), 22 from the rendition table (9,465 uses), 0 from the fallback under the tokenizer reader, 14 unmapped (590 uses)

results.name: unmapped_control_words
results.note: uses; neither a macro nor matched by a terminal of the baseline grammar

conclusion: The tokenizer reader gives the spike reader's table on 56 pages and adds \P on the 22 that define it by \renewcommand; every macro used in math is defined on its own page, so the fallback map is never needed on Siegrist, and no key or parse changes on this corpus because the fallback body agrees. M01's reader is the tokenizer reader (D4 M01); the bodies that differ between pages (\var, \kur, \skw, \sgn) confirm per-rendition tables (HTML-06).
